paragraphs: We are a leader and one of the most geographically diverse operators in the theatrical exhibition industry. As of December 31, 2025, we operated 496 theaters and 5,637 screens in the United States, or "U.S.", and Latin America. Our U.S. circuit operated 303 theaters and 4,241 screens and our Latin America circuit operated 193 theaters and 1,396 screens across 13 countries. Our significant and diverse presence in the U.S. and Latin America has made us an important distribution channel for movie studios and other content providers. We believe our portfolio of high-quality theaters with multiple platforms and amenities provides a preferred destination for moviegoers.
As of December 31, 2025, we managed our business under two reportable segments: U.S. markets and international markets. See Note 20 to the consolidated financial statements.

The success of the theatrical exhibition industry is contingent upon several key factors, including the volume of new film and other content available, the box office performance of new film content released, the duration of the exclusive theatrical release window, and evolving consumer behavior with competition from other forms of in-and-out-of home entertainment.
Preliminary estimates indicate that North American industry box office revenues were approximately $8.9 billion for 2025.

Films leading the box office during the year ended December 31, 2025 included A Minecraft Movie, Lilo & Stitch, Superman, Jurassic World: Rebirth, Zootopia 2, Wicked: For Good, Sinners, The Fantastic Four: First Steps, How to Train Your Dragon, and Avatar: Fire and Ash, among other films.

Films scheduled for release in 2026 include The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Avengers: Doomsday, Toy Story 5, Minions 3, Moana, The Mandalorian & Grogu, The Odyssey, Jumanji 3 and Dune: Part Three, among other films.
Preliminary estimates for Latin American industry box office revenues in the countries where we operate were approximately $1.2 billion for 2025.

Box office performance in Latin America is dependent upon the quantity, quality and timing of Hollywood film product, and to a lesser extent, alternative content and local film product. Specific to Hollywood content, some topics, characters, and franchises may resonate differently with Latin American audiences, leading certain films to over or under index relative to North America. Box office performance in Latin American markets is also impacted by political, economic and social conditions, growing populations in select markets, and continued retail development.
We believe the long-term fundamentals of our industry remain intact:

Consumers Remain Enthusiastic for Theatrical Movie-Going. Consumer enthusiasm for theatrical movie-going remains evident, as audiences consistently engage with compelling content across genres and audience segments. Although box office performance and attendance levels can fluctuate depending on the volume and mix of film releases, the theatrical experience continues to hold a meaningful place in consumer entertainment preferences.

A Theatrical Release Enhances a Film's Promotional Impact and Overall Asset Value. Theatrical exhibition has long been the primary distribution channel for launching new major film releases. A theatrical release provides an enhanced promotional platform for filmed entertainment content by heightening its exposure, increasing its perceived quality, strengthening recall, and driving greater viewing interest. Furthermore, experiencing content in a shared theatrical environment elevates emotions and engagement with stories and characters, which builds larger brands, franchises, and cultural moments. The theatrical release of a film generates the initial revenue stream, driving performance in downstream distribution channels, including streaming, which enhances overall asset value.

Resilient Industry Across Technology Innovations and Economic Cycles. Theatrical movie-going remains one of the most convenient and affordable forms of out-of-home entertainment. As such, it has proven resilient during inflationary and recessionary periods and across various technological innovations, including VHS, internet, DVD and streaming. For example, North American industry box office grew in six of the last eight recessions.
Our strategic objectives prioritize experiential consumer-based, revenue-generating, and productivity-driving initiatives, including:

Deliver an Extraordinary Guest Experience. We aim to differentiate our theaters through consistent investment in high-demand consumer amenities that provide a larger-than-life, cinematic entertainment experience with top-notch guest service. Examples of amenities include state-of-the-art sight and sound technology, premium large format auditoriums, recliners, and motion seats, as well as expansive food and beverage offerings. We believe our ongoing focus on providing an extraordinary guest experience is a primary factor of our consistent industry-leading results.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business, Economic, Market and Operating Conditions
A variety of uncontrollable events may disrupt our businesses, reduce guest attendance, or increase the cost or reduce the profitability of providing our products and services.
Our business depends on film production and performance.
Our results of operations may be impacted by the reduction of exclusive theatrical windows
Our results of operations fluctuate on a seasonal basis.
A deterioration in relationships with content distributors could adversely affect our ability to obtain commercially successful content.
We face intense competition for patrons and films which may adversely affect our business.
An increase in competing forms of entertainment or the use of alternative film distribution channels may reduce movie theater attendance and limit revenue growth.
Our foreign operations are subject to adverse regulations, economic instability and currency exchange risk.
Labor market conditions, loss of key personnel, or inability for our workforce to scale as business evolves may negatively impact our operations and operating results.
We are subject to impairment losses due to potential declines in the fair value of our assets.
Risks Related to Financing and Liquidity
We have substantial long-term lease and debt obligations, which may restrict our ability to fund current and future operations and that restrict our ability to enter into certain transactions.
A lowering or withdrawal of the ratings assigned or a change in outlook to our outstanding debt securities by rating agencies may increase our future borrowing costs and impact our access to capital.
A credit market crisis may adversely affect our ability to raise capital and may materially impact our operations.
Holdings' ability to pay dividends may be limited or otherwise restricted.
Future sales of Holdings' common stock may adversely affect the prevailing market price.
We are subject to various government regulations which could result in substantial costs.
We may face data protection, data security, and privacy risks in connection with privacy regulation.
We may be subject to increased labor and benefits costs.
Provisions in Holdings' corporate documents and certain of CUSA's agreements, as well as Delaware law, may hinder a change of control.
Risks Related to Information Security and Business Disruptions
An information security incident, including a cyber security breach, and our failure to protect our electronically stored data could adversely affect our business or reputation.
A failure to adapt to future technological innovations could impact our ability to compete effectively and could adversely affect our results of operations.
Legislative or regulatory initiatives related to global warming/climate change concerns may negatively impact our business.
We may be subject to liability under environmental laws and regulations.
Product recalls and associated costs could adversely affect our reputation and financial condition.
Our business, financial condition and results of operations may be adversely impacted by the effects of inflation.
paragraphs: An investment in Holdings' common stock or our debt securities involves risks and uncertainties, and our actual results and future trends may differ materially from our past or projected future performance. We urge investors to consider carefully the risk factors described below, in addition to the other information contained in this report, in evaluating our Company and our business. It is not possible to identify all risk factors, and additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial may also materially impact our business operations.

Our results of operations can be significantly and adversely affected in the U.S., Latin America or in specific regions as a result of a variety of factors beyond our control, including: health concerns (such as health emergencies, endemics, epidemics and pandemics); adverse weather conditions arising from short-term weather patterns or long-term climate change, including catastrophic events or natural disasters such as hurricanes, typhoons, floods, droughts, wildfires and earthquakes; international, political or military developments, including trade and other international disputes and social unrest resulting in supply chain interruptions and increased tariffs and other costs; macroeconomic conditions, including a decline in economic activity, inflation, deflation and foreign exchange rate fluctuations; and terrorist attacks. These events and others, such as rising energy costs and computer virus attacks, intrusions, ransom ware or other widespread computing or telecommunications failures, may also damage our ability to provide our services.

We maintain insurance coverage against the risk of losses relating to some of these events, generally including certain physical damage to our property and resulting business interruption, cybersecurity events, certain injuries occurring on our property and some liabilities for alleged breach of legal responsibilities. When insurance is obtained it is subject to deductibles, exclusions, terms, conditions and limits of liability. The types and levels of coverage we obtain vary from time to time depending on our view of the likelihood of specific types and levels of loss compared to the cost of obtaining coverage for such types and levels of loss. We may experience material losses not covered by our insurance. The costs of protecting against such incidents may impact the results of our operations.

Our business depends on the availability and performance of films for theatrical exhibition. Our industry relies on a consistent cadence of high-quality, wide-release films with broad consumer appeal. A reduced volume of new film releases, weaker film performance, or less effective marketing support can adversely affect attendance and revenue. Film production and release schedules may be disrupted by reductions in financing and production, as well as by labor actions such as strikes or work stoppages involving directors, writers, actors, or other industry groups. For example, the 2023 work stoppages by the Writers Guild of America and SAG-AFTRA delayed the production and release of certain films. Contract expirations for the WGA, DGA, and SAG‑AFTRA are scheduled again in 2026, and any related work stoppages could similarly delay future film releases.

The volume of new theatrical content has improved but has not returned to historical levels and may not fully recover, which could materially impact our business. Consolidation among major studios and evolving distribution strategies may further limit film availability, increase distributors' bargaining power, or change the terms under which we license films. Certain distributors have also released titles exclusively or primarily in select premium formats, which can reduce the number of commercially viable titles available for our circuit and negatively impact attendance and revenue. Studios may additionally designate certain content for direct‑to‑streaming release, reducing the number of titles available for theatrical exhibition.

The exclusive theatrical window ("window") refers to the period during which a film is exclusively available in theaters before it becomes accessible through in-home distribution channels, such as digital rental and/or sell-through (eg: PVOD, PEST), streaming services, television and physical media. This window remains a significant driver of box office performance and supports the overall value of the theatrical experience.

paragraphs: Cinemark Holdings, Inc. ("Holdings") is a holding company and its wholly-owned subsidiary is Cinemark USA, Inc. Holdings consolidates Cinemark USA, Inc. and its subsidiaries, or "CUSA", for financial statement purposes. CUSA's operating revenue and operating expenses comprise nearly 100% of Holdings' revenue and operating expenses. As such, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations ("MD&A") that follows is for Holdings and CUSA in all material respects, unless otherwise noted. Differences between the operations and results of Holdings and CUSA are separately disclosed and explained. Where it is important to distinguish between Holdings and CUSA, specific reference is made to either Holdings or CUSA. Otherwise, all references to "we," "our," "us," "the Company" or "Cinemark" relate to Cinemark Holdings, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries.

The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with the financial statements and accompanying notes included in this report. This discussion may contain forward-looking statements. See "Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" and "Risk Factors" for a discussion of the uncertainties and risks associated with these statements. Discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for 2024 compared with 2023 is included in Item 7 of the Company's 2024 Annual Report on Form 10-K filed on February 16, 2024.

We are a leader in the theatrical exhibition industry, with theaters in the U.S., Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Peru, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Panama, Guatemala, Bolivia, and Paraguay. As of December 31, 2025, we managed our business under two reportable segments – U.S. markets and international markets. See Note 20 to the consolidated financial statements.

The success of the theatrical exhibition industry is contingent upon several key factors, including the volume of new film content available, the box office performance of new film content released, the duration of the exclusive theatrical release window, and evolving consumer behavior with competition from other forms of in-and-out-of-home entertainment.

We generate revenue primarily from filmed entertainment box office receipts and concession sales, with additional revenue from screen advertising, screen rental and other revenue streams, such as transactional fees, studio trailer placements, promotional income, meeting rentals, and games located in some of our facilities. Filmed entertainment box office receipts include traditional content from studios as well as alternative entertainment, such as foreign and faith-based films, concert events, and other special events in our theaters. NCM provides our domestic theaters with various forms of in-theater advertising. Our Flix Media subsidiaries provide screen advertising and alternative content for our international circuit and for other international exhibitors.

Films released during the year ended December 31, 2025 included A Minecraft Movie, Lilo & Stitch, Superman, Jurassic World: Rebirth, Zootopia 2, Wicked: For Good, Sinners, The Fantastic Four: First Steps, How to Train Your Dragon, and Avatar: Fire and Ash, among other films.

Films scheduled for release in 2026 include The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Avengers: Doomsday, Toy Story 5, Minions 3, Moana, The Mandalorian & Grogu, The Odyssey, Jumanji 3 and Dune: Part Three, among other films.

Film rental costs are variable in nature and fluctuate with our admissions revenue. Film rental costs as a percentage of revenue are generally higher for periods in which more blockbuster films are released. Advertising costs, which are expensed as incurred, are primarily related to expanding our customer base, increasing the frequency of visits and growing loyalty. These expenses vary depending on the timing and length of such campaigns.

Concession supplies expense is variable in nature and fluctuates with our concession revenue and product mix. Inflationary pressures and tariffs continue to impact product costs in the near term and may impact product costs going forward. We source products from a variety of global partners to minimize supply chain interruptions and manage costs, wherever possible.

Although salaries and wages include a fixed cost component (i.e., the minimum staffing costs to operate a theater facility during non-peak periods), salaries and wages tend to move in relation to anticipated changes in attendance.

Staffing levels may vary based on the amenities offered at each location, such as full-service restaurants, bars or expanded food and beverage options. In certain international locations, staffing levels are also subject to local regulations, including minimum hour requirements. Labor market conditions and inflationary pressures have driven increases in wage rates and benefits across our labor base and similar increases may continue in the future.

Facility lease expense is primarily a fixed cost at the theater level as most of our facility leases require a fixed monthly minimum rent payment. Certain leases are subject to percentage rent only, while others are subject to percentage rent in addition to their fixed monthly rent if a target annual performance level is achieved. Facility lease expense as a percentage of revenue is also affected by the number of theaters under operating leases, the number of theaters under finance leases and the number of owned theaters.

Utilities and other costs include both fixed and variable costs and primarily consist of utilities, property taxes, property insurance, janitorial costs, credit card fees, third party ticket sales commissions, gift card commissions, repairs and maintenance expenses, security services, and projection and sound equipment maintenance expenses.

General and administrative expenses to support the overall management of the Company are primarily fixed in nature. Fixed expenses include salaries, wages and benefits costs for our corporate office personnel, facility expenses for our corporate and other offices, software license and maintenance costs and audit fees. General and administrative expenses also include some variable expenses such as incentive compensation, consulting and legal fees, general supplies, and other costs that are not specifically associated with the operations of our theaters.

paragraphs: 本公司為戲劇展演業的重要領導者，且為該產業中地理分佈最廣的營運者之一。截至2025年12月31日，本公司於美國（"U.S."）及拉丁美洲運營496間戲院與5,637個銀幕。本公司美國電影院線運營303間戲院與4,241個銀幕，本公司拉丁美洲電影院線運營193間戲院與1,396個銀幕，遍及13個國家。本公司在美國與拉丁美洲的重要且多樣化的存在，使其成為電影製片廠及其他內容供應商的重要分銷渠道。本公司相信，擁有高品質戲院與多種平台及設施的組合，為電影觀眾提供了優先的選擇。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司將業務分為兩個應報告分部：美國市場與國際市場。詳見財務報表附註第20項。
戲劇展演產業的成功取決於多項關鍵因素，包括新電影及其他內容的數量、新電影內容在票房的表現、獨佔戲院上映窗口的持續時間，以及消費者行為的變化與其他形式的居家與外出行娛樂的競爭。
初步預估顯示，北美產業票房收入於2025年約為89億美元。
截至2025年12月31日，票房表現居前的電影包括《Minecraft電影》、《Lilo & Stitch》、《超人》、《侏羅紀世界：重生》、《Zootopia 2》、《Wicked: For Good》、《Sinners》、《神奇四俠：第一步》、《如何訓練你的龍》以及《阿凡達：火與灰》，以及其他電影。
預計於2026年上映的電影包括《Super Mario Galaxy電影》、《蜘蛛人：全新日出》、《復仇者：末日》、《玩具總動員5》、《Minions 3》、《Moana》、《曼達洛人與Grogu》、《奧德賽》、《Jumanji 3》以及《沙丘：第三部》，以及其他電影。
初步預估顯示，本公司運營國家的拉丁美洲產業票房收入於2025年約為12億美元。
拉丁美洲市場的票房表現取決於好萊塢電影產品的數量、品質與時機，以及較少程度的替代內容與本地電影產品。針對好萊塢內容，某些主題、角色與系列可能與拉丁美洲觀眾產生不同的共鳴，導致某些電影相對於北美市場過度或不足地表現。拉丁美洲市場的票房表現也受到政治、經濟與社會條件、特定市場人口成長，以及持續的零售發展的影響。
我們相信我們產業的長期基本面仍然完整：
消費者持續熱衷於電影院觀賞電影。消費者對電影院觀賞電影的熱情仍然明顯，因為觀眾持續參與各類型及各目標羣體的精彩內容。雖然票房表現與觀眾人數會根據電影發行的數量與組合而有所波動，但電影院的體驗仍然在消費者娛樂偏好中佔有重要地位。

電影院發行能提升電影的宣傳效果與整體資產價值。電影院放映一直是發行重大電影的新作的主要分銷渠道。電影院發行能為電影娛樂內容提供更強的宣傳平台，透過提高曝光度、增加其被認為的品質、強化記憶、並驅動更高的觀賞興趣。此外，在共享的電影院環境中體驗內容能提升情感與對故事與角色的投入，這有助於建立更大的品牌、系列與文化時刻。電影的電影院發行產生最初的收入來源，驅動後續分銷渠道的表現，包括串流，這會提升整體資產價值。
產業在技術創新與經濟週期中表現堅韌。電影院觀賞仍然是最方便且經濟的戶外娛樂形式之一。因此，在通貨膨脹與經濟衰退時期，以及各種技術創新，包括VHS、互聯網、DVD與串流的時代，產業都表現出強韌性。例如，北美產業票房在過去八次經濟衰退中有六次成長。
我們的戰略目標優先考量以消費者體驗為基礎、能產生收入、並能提升生產力的計畫，包括：
提供卓越的顧客體驗。我們旨在透過持續投資高需求的消費者設施，來區隔我們的電影院，提供大於現實的電影娛樂體驗與優質的顧客服務。設施範例包括最先進的視聽科技、豪華大型格式劇院、躺椅、動感座椅，以及廣泛的餐飲選擇。我們相信我們持續專注於提供卓越的顧客體驗，是我們持續領先產業的關鍵因素。

paragraphs: Cinemark Holdings, Inc. ("Holdings") 為一間控股公司，其全資子公司為 Cinemark USA, Inc. Holdings 為財務報表目的，將 Cinemark USA, Inc. 及其子公司，或 "CUSA"，納入合併財務報表。CUSA 的營運收入及營運費用約佔 Holdings 的收入及營運費用的 100%。因此，後述的管理層討論與分析財務狀況及營運結果 ("MD&A") 係針對 Holdings 及 CUSA，除非另有說明。Holdings 與 CUSA 之間的營運及結果差異會分別說明與披露。在需要區分 Holdings 與 CUSA 時，會明確提及 Holdings 或 CUSA。否則，所有提及 "we," "our," "us," "the Company" 或 "Cinemark" 均指 Cinemark Holdings, Inc. 及其合併子公司。
後述的討論與分析應與本報告所附的財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。此討論可能包含前瞻性陳述。請參閱 "前瞻性陳述警示聲明" 及 "風險因素"，以瞭解與這些陳述相關的不確定性與風險。有關本公司 2024 年財務狀況及營運結果與 2,023 年比較的討論，請參閱本公司於 2024 年 2 月 16 日提交的 10-K 年度報告第 7 項。
我們是電影院業的領導者，在美國、巴西、阿根廷、智利、哥倫比亞、祕魯、洪都拉斯、薩爾瓦多、尼加拉瓜、哥斯達黎加、巴拿馬、危地馬拉、玻利維亞及巴拉圭等地設有電影院。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的業務分為兩個應報告分部 – 美國市場與國際市場。請參閱合併財務報表附註 20。
電影院業的成功取決於多個關鍵因素，包括新電影內容的數量、新電影內容的票房表現、獨家電影院上映窗口的長度，以及消費者行為的變化與其他形式的居家與外出行娛樂的競爭。

我們的收入主要來自電影娛樂票房收入及場內販售收入，另有來自螢幕廣告、螢幕租賃及其他收入來源，例如交易費用、製片廠預告片置放、促銷收入、會議租賃及部分場館內的遊戲收入。電影娛樂票房收入包括來自製片廠的傳統內容，以及替代性娛樂，例如外語電影及基於信仰的電影、音樂會活動及其他特殊活動。NCM 為我們的國內電影院提供多種場內廣告形式。我們的 Flix Media 子公司為我們的國際戲院網及其他國際戲院提供螢幕廣告及替代性內容。
2025 年度截至 12 月 31 日所發行的電影包括《Minecraft 動畫電影》、《Lilo & Stitch》、《超人》、《侏羅紀世界：重生》、《動物森友會 2》、《Wicked: For Good》、《Sinners》、《神奇四俠：第一步》、《如何訓練你的龍》及《阿凡達：火與灰》，以及其他電影。
預計於 2026 年發行的電影包括《Super Mario Galaxy 動畫電影》、《蜘蛛人：全新日出》、《復仇者：末日》、《玩具總動員 5》、《Minions 3》、《Moana》、《曼達洛人與 Grogu》、《奧德賽》、《Jumanji 3》及《沙丘：第三部》，以及其他電影。
電影租賃費用為變動性費用，會隨著我們的入場收入而波動。電影租賃費用佔收入的百分比，在發行更多票房大片的期間通常較高。廣告費用為發生時即計入費用，主要與擴大客戶羣、提高造訪頻率及提升忠誠度有關。這些費用會根據活動的時間及長度而有所不同。
concession supplies expense 是變動性成本，會隨著我們的 concession 收入及產品組成而變動。通貨膨脹壓力及關稅持續影響產品成本，在近期內可能影響產品成本，未來也可能持續影響產品成本。我們從多種全球夥伴處取得產品，以減少供應鏈中斷並盡可能管理成本。
雖然薪資及工資包含固定成本組成（即，運作劇院設施於非高峯期間的最低人力成本），但薪資及工資通常會隨著預期的入場人數變動而變動。
人力配置可能因各據點所提供的設施而有所不同，例如全服務餐廳、酒吧或擴充的餐飲選項。在某些國際據點，人力配置也受到當地法規的影響，包括最低工時要求。勞動市場條件及通貨膨脹壓力已導致我們勞動基數的工資率及福利增加，未來也可能持續增加。
設施租賃費用在劇院層面主要是固定成本，因為我們大多數的設施租賃需要支付固定的每月最低租金。某些租賃僅適用百分比租金，而其他租賃則在達成目標年度營運績效時，除了固定每月租金外，還適用百分比租金。設施租賃費用佔營業收入的百分比也受到在經營租賃下的劇院數量、在財務租賃下的劇院數量以及自有劇院數量的影響。
電力及其它費用包含固定及變動成本，主要由電力、財產稅、財產保險、清潔費用、信用卡手續費、第三方票務銷售佣金、禮品卡佣金、修繕及維護費用、安全服務及投影與音響設備維護費用組成。
支持本公司整體管理的總務及行政費用主要是固定性質。固定費用包括我們總部人員的薪資、工資及福利成本、總部及其他辦公室的設施費用、軟體授權及維護費用及審計費用。總務及行政費用也包含一些變動費用，例如績效獎金、顧問及法律費用、一般辦公用品及其它與我們劇院營運無直接關聯的費用。

headings: 與本公司業務、經濟、市場及營運環境相關之風險
許多無法控制之事件可能幹擾本公司業務、減少觀眾人數，或提高提供產品與服務之成本或降低其獲利能力。
本公司業務依賴電影製作與演出。
本公司營運結果可能受獨家戲院上映窗口縮短之影響。
本公司營運結果會因季節性因素而波動。
與內容發行商之關係惡化可能不利於本公司取得商業成功之內容。
本公司面臨對觀眾與電影之激烈競爭，可能不利於本公司業務。
競品娛樂形式增加或使用替代性電影發行渠道，可能減少電影院觀眾人數並限制收入成長。
本公司之海外營運面臨不利之法規、經濟不穩定及貨幣兌換風險。
勞動市場狀況、失去關鍵人員或本公司員工無法隨著業務發展而擴充規模，可能對本公司營運及營運成果產生負面影響。
本公司因潛在資產公允價值下降而面臨減損損失。
與融資及流動性相關之風險
本公司有大量長期租賃及債務義務，可能限制本公司資助目前及未來營運之能力，並限制本公司進行特定交易之能力。
信用評等機構對本公司發行之債務證券所給予之評等降低或撤回，或對本公司發行之債務證券之展望看法改變，可能提高本公司未來借款成本，並影響本公司取得資金之能力。
信用市場危機可能對本公司籌資能力產生不利影響，並可能對本公司營運產生重大影響。
Holdings 之能力可能受到限制，無法支付股息或受到其他限制。
本公司普通股未來之銷售可能不利於現行市場價格。
本公司受各種政府法規之制約，可能導致重大成本。
本公司可能因隱私權法規而面臨資料保護、資料安全及隱私權相關風險。
本公司可能因勞動及福利成本增加而受影響。
Holdings 之公司文件條款及 CUSA 之部分協議，以及特拉華州法規，可能阻礙控制權之變更。
與資訊安全及營運中斷相關之風險
資訊安全事件，包括網路安全違規，以及本公司未能保護電子儲存資料，可能對本公司營運或聲譽造成不利影響。
未能適應未來的科技創新可能影響我們競爭的能力，並可能對我們的營運結果產生負面影響。
與全球變暖/氣候變遷相關的立法或監管措施可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
我們可能因違反環境法規而面臨法律責任。
產品回收及相關成本可能對我們的聲譽及財務狀況產生負面影響。
我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果可能因通貨膨脹的影響而受到負面影響。
paragraphs: 投資 Holdings 普通股或我們的債務證券涉及風險與不確定性，我們的實際結果與未來趨勢可能與我們過去或預期的未來表現有重大差異。我們敦促投資人仔細考慮下列風險因素，並參考本報告中包含的其他資訊，以評估本公司與我們的業務。無法識別所有風險因素，且目前未知或我們認為不重要的其他風險與不確定性，也可能對我們的業務運作產生重大影響。

我們的營運結果可能因美國、拉丁美洲或特定地區的多種因素而受到顯著且不利的影響，這些因素超出我們的控制範圍，包括：健康問題（例如健康危機、地方性傳染病、流行病與大流行病）；因短暫天氣模式或長期氣候變遷而產生的不利天氣條件，包括災難性事件或自然災害，例如颶風、颱風、洪水、乾旱、野火與地震；國際、政治或軍事發展，包括貿易及其他國際爭議與社會動亂，導致供應鏈中斷與增加關稅及其他成本；總體經濟條件，包括經濟活動減少、通貨膨脹、通貨緊縮與外匯匯率波動；以及恐怖攻擊。這些事件及其他因素，例如能源成本上升與電腦病毒攻擊、入侵、勒索軟體或其他廣泛的計算機或電信業者失敗，也可能損害我們提供服務的能力。

我們針對與這些事件相關的損失風險維持保險覆蓋，通常包括某些物理損壞至我們財產及由此導致的業務中斷、網路安全事件、某些在我們財產上發生的傷害以及一些因涉嫌違反法律責任而產生的賠償責任。當取得保險時，保險會受到免賠額、除外責任、條款、條件及賠償責任上限的限制。我們取得的保險種類與層級會根據我們對特定類型與層級損失的可能性評估與取得該類型與層級損失保險的成本而有所變動。我們可能遭遇未被保險覆蓋的重大損失。防範這些事件的成本可能影響我們的營運結果。

我們的業務依賴於電影在戲院的放映。我們的產業依賴於高品質、廣泛發行且具有廣泛消費者吸引力的電影。新電影發行數量減少、電影表現較弱或市場推廣支援不足，可能對觀眾人數與營收產生不利影響。電影製片與發行排期可能因資金減少與製片減少，以及導演、作家、演員或其他產業團體的罷工等勞動行動而受到幹擾。例如，2023 年美國作家協會與 SAG-AFTRA 的罷工行動延遲了某些電影的製片與發行。WGA、DGA 與 S&A-GAFTRA 的合約到期日預計在 2026 年，任何相關的罷工行動也可能同樣延遲未來的電影發行。

新戲院內容的數量已改善，但尚未回到歷史水平，且可能無法完全恢復，這可能會對我們的業務產生重大影響。主要製片廠之間的併購與發行策略的變化，可能進一步限制電影的可得性、增加發行商的議價能力，或改變我們 licence 電影的條件。某些發行商也已將部分作品獨家或主要在特定高階格式中發行，這會減少我們戲院可使用的商業可行作品數量，並對觀眾人數與營收產生負面影響。製片廠也可能將某些內容指定為直接串流發行，減少可供戲院放映的電影數量。
獨家戲院窗口（"window"）指的是電影在戲院獨家放映的期間，直到其透過居家發行渠道（如數位租賃及/或銷售（例如 PVOD、PEST）、串流服務、電視與實體媒體）可取得為止。這個窗口仍是票房表現的重要驅動力，並支撐整體戲院體驗的價值。
